name: אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ
summary: Three men: David’s fourth son, born of Haggith in Hebron, who exalted himself to be king while David still lived, was spared by Solomon and then put to death for asking for Abishag; a Levite whom Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah; and a chief of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day. The name is אֲדֹנִי “my lord” with the divine name in its short forms, ‑יָּהוּ and ‑יָּה (both spellings are used of David’s son): a sentence, “my lord is Yahweh”, the confession of Psalm 16:2. The story of David’s son turns on who is lord: Nathan sets “Adonijah reigns” against “our lord David does not know it”, and Adonijah himself owns that the kingdom became Solomon’s “from Yahweh”.

evidence.note: Of David’s sons born in Hebron: “the fourth, אֲדֹנִיָּה the son of Haggith”.
“אֲדֹנִיָּה the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king.”
Nathan: “Have you not heard that אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ has become king, and our lord (אֲדֹנֵינוּ) David does not know it?” The name and the word it is made of, side by side.
He feared Solomon and took hold of the horns of the altar.
“The kingdom turned and became my brother’s, for it was his from Yahweh.”
Solomon: “today אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ shall be put to death”; Benaiah fell on him and he died.
Among the Levites sent with the book of the law: וַאֲדֹנִיָּהוּ. The same verse has the name טוֹב אֲדוֹנִיָּה, “good is my lord Yah”.
אֲדֹנִיָּה among the heads of the people who sealed.
The name as a sentence: “I said to Yahweh, You are my Lord.”

note: TIPNR’s key for the man of Neh 10:17 uses the English verse number (Neh.10.16). The i of אֲדֹנִי is read as “my”, as in אֲדֹנִי everywhere; it could be the old joining vowel of names (as in מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק), giving “Yah is lord”, with no change to what the name confesses. Phoenician builds the same name with its own god: ʾdnbʿl, “Baal is my lord” (Krahmalkov p. 34), which is why phn-adn is named.
